summary: The patch rewrites SSTable.delete() so it sorts components by File.lastModified() and deletes them oldest first. Checklists applied: absence.md and completeness.md under refdir. Tier small, whole diff read, nothing left unreviewed. Searches found that the caller LogTransaction.SSTableTidier still deletes the DATA file before calling SSTable.delete(). So the main scenario in the ticket is not fixed. The patch also changes failure semantics by swapping FileUtils.deleteWithConfirm for FileUtils.delete. It adds no test, although the ticket's test plan names LogTransactionTest additions. I did not review LogFile or LogRecord beyond reading verifyRecord and make() to confirm what the REMOVE record timestamp covers.

findings.rule: Fix-patch mode: did the fix reach every path that causes the original bug? (parallel path coverage)
findings.problem: SSTableTidier.run() still calls delete(datafile) on the DATA file at line 396, before it calls SSTable.delete(desc, ...) at line 401. SSTable.delete() is only reached after DATA is already gone, so the new timestamp sort cannot put DATA in order. This is the exact scenario in the ticket. DATA is usually not the newest file, so it is not always safe to delete it first. If the node crashes after the DATA delete and before the remaining deletes finish, the newest non-STATS file (for example the Index, Filter or TOC file written after DATA) survives. On restart LogFile.verifyRecord() compares the REMOVE record's updateTime with the on-disk files, finds them different, marks the record invalid, and the node refuses to start. Because the DATA delete is untouched, the crash window the ticket describes is still open for ordinary compaction cleanup. SSTable.delete() is called from nowhere else in src/java, so the sorted delete only affects the tail of the sequence.
findings.fix: Remove the special-case DATA delete in SSTableTidier.run(). Keep the retry-on-failure behaviour by letting SSTable.delete() throw, or have SSTable.delete() own the whole ordered deletion including DATA. At the least, make the tidier delete DATA only when it is the oldest file.

findings.rule: API contract: changed exception and return behaviour that callers rely on
findings.problem: The loop now calls FileUtils.delete(String), which returns File.delete() and swallows failure. The old code used FileUtils.deleteWithConfirm, which throws FSWriteError when a delete fails. SSTableTidier relies on that exception: the catch in LogTransaction.java around line 403 adds the tidier to failedDeletions so the deletion is retried after GC. Trigger: any non-DATA component cannot be deleted, for example because of a Windows-style open handle, a permissions error or an I/O error. SSTable.delete() now returns true and the tidier treats the sstable as deleted. It also decrements totalDiskSpaceUsed, so the leaked files are never retried and metrics go wrong. A partial delete that is not retried can also leave the on-disk state out of step with the REMOVE record. The SUMMARY component was previously deleted with the non-confirming FileUtils.delete, but every other component was confirmed. The patch drops confirmation for all of them.
findings.fix: Use FileUtils.deleteWithConfirm(desc.filenameFor(component)) in the sorted loop for every component. If SUMMARY should stay lenient, keep a lenient delete for that one component only.

findings.rule: Refactor aftermath: new behaviour needs a test, as the ticket's test plan requires
findings.problem: The diff touches only SSTable.java. The ticket's test plan calls for additions to LogTransactionTest, for example a test that deletes an SSTable's components in order and then verifies the REMOVE record, or that simulates a partial delete. Nothing guards the ordering contract, and nothing would have caught that the tidier deletes DATA before SSTable.delete() runs (cs-1). Timestamp ties are not specified either: files with equal lastModified keep set iteration order from the Set<Component>, and a missing file returns lastModified 0 and sorts first. A test should cover both cases.
findings.fix: Add LogTransactionTest cases that give components distinct, controlled lastModified values (including STATS and DATA being oldest or newest). Run the real tidier path, interrupt it after the first delete, and assert that LogFile.verifyRecord() still passes.

findings.rule: Stale comments and javadoc after a behaviour change
findings.problem: The comment says 'Because we delete files from oldest to newest, the latest update time should always match.' Now that SSTable.delete() enforces the order, the comment should name that mechanism. It should also say that the STATS file is excluded from the REMOVE timestamp (LogRecord.make with includeStatsFile=false) and that the tidier's separate DATA delete is a known exception until cs-1 is fixed. SSTable.java also has no javadoc stating the ordering guarantee for callers.
findings.fix: Add javadoc to SSTable.delete() stating that components are deleted in ascending lastModified order. Update the verifyRecord comment to point at it.
